```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** (tmux is Session → Window → Pane). "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
23	
24	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
27	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
28	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
29	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
30	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
31	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
32	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
33	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
34	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
35	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
36	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
37	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
38	
39	## Keybindings
40	
41	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
42	
43	| Key | Action | Type |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
46	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
47	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
48	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
49	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
50	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
51	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
52	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
53	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
54	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
55	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
56	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
57	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
58	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
59	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
60	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
61	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
62	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
63	
64	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
65	
66	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
67	
68	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
69	
70	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
71	
72	```bash
73	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
74	```
75	
76	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
77	
78	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
79	
80	## Television integration
81	
82	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
83	
84	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
85	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
86	
87	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
88	
89	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
90	
91	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
92	
93	```bash
94	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
95	```
96	
97	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
98	
99	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
100	
101	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
102	
103	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
106	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
107	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
108	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
109	
110	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
111	
112	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
113	
114	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
115	
116	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
117	
118	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
119	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
120	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
121	
122	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.

4	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:

6	#   sesh-root / sroot   — session at the current git root (or $PWD)

13	# Shell wiring (the keybinding layer is per-shell):
14	#   zsh : ZLE widget + bindkey '\es'        → dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh
15	#   bash: ble.sh `ble-bind -x 'M-s'`         → dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash.tmpl

23	# Sesh session picker (fzf-tmux + sesh list).
24	# Called as a normal function in either shell; the zsh widget and the bash
25	# ble-bind callback both just invoke this. Prompt redraw on exit is handled
26	# by whatever widget engine invoked us (zle / ble.sh) — no explicit reset.
27	function sesh-sessions() {
28	    {
29	        exec </dev/tty
30	        exec <&1
31	        local session
32	        session=$(sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
33	            --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
34	            --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
35	            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
36	            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
37	            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
38	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
39	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
40	            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
41	            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
42	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
43	            --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
44	        )
45	        [ -z "$session" ] && return
46	        sesh connect "$session"
47	    }
48	}

50	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	#
52	# All helpers below take care to avoid the lowercase `path` / `cdpath` /
53	# `manpath` / `fpath` zsh-tied-array trap (see
54	# pitfalls/zsh-tied-array-path-shadowing.md).

56	# Resolve the git repo root, or return non-zero if not in a repo.
57	function _sesh_git_root() {

59	}

61	# Sanitize a string for use as a tmux session name.
62	# tmux forbids `.` and `:` in session names; we also strip whitespace.
63	function _sesh_sanitize() {
64	    printf '%s\n' "${1//[.:[:space:]]/-}"
65	}

67	# Switch to or attach to a tmux session named $1 (creating it at $2 if needed).
68	# Inside tmux: `switch-client`. Outside tmux: `attach-session`.
69	function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {
70	    local session="$1"
71	    if [ -n "$TMUX" ]; then
72	        tmux switch-client -t "$session"
73	    else
74	        tmux attach-session -t "$session"
75	    fi
76	}

78	# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
79	# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
80	# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)
81	function _sesh_ensure_session() {
82	    local session="$1" target="$2"
83	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
84	        return 0   # already exists
85	    fi
86	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"
87	    return 1       # newly created
88	}

90	# Wrap a known specstory provider in `specstory run X` so the agent picks up
91	# auto-save markdown logging. Bare CLI names that aren't specstory providers
92	# (currently: opencode — see backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md) pass
93	# through unchanged.
94	#
95	# Update the case list when specstory adds providers (track upstream:
96	# specstoryai/getspecstory#146 for opencode, similar issues for others).
97	#
98	# Args: $1=agent, $2=specstory_mode (auto|never; default auto)
99	#   auto  — wrap if known provider, raw otherwise (the historical default)
100	#   never — pass through raw regardless (CLI flag --no-specstory sets this)
101	function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
102	    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
103	    if [ "$specstory_mode" = "never" ]; then
104	        # Even an empty agent goes raw → caller's responsibility to pick a
105	        # sensible default (we choose `claude` upstream when --no-specstory
106	        # is set, since `specstory run` with no arg defaults to claude too).
107	        printf '%s\n' "${agent:-claude}"
108	        return
109	    fi
110	    case "$agent" in
111	        ""|"specstory")
112	            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
113	            printf '%s\n' "specstory run"
114	            ;;
115	        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
116	            printf '%s\n' "specstory run $agent"
117	            ;;
118	        *)
119	            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
120	            # later as specstory adds support).
121	            printf '%s\n' "$agent"
122	            ;;
123	    esac
124	}

126	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
127	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
128	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
129	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
130	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
131	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
132	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
133	#             land in shell.
134	#
135	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
136	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
137	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
138	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
139	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
140	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
141	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
142	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
143	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
144	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
145	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
146	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
147	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
148	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
149	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
150	    case "$mode" in
151	        kill)
152	            printf '%s\n' "$inner"
153	            ;;
154	        restart)
155	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
156	            printf '%s\n' "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
157	            ;;
158	        shell|*)
159	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
160	            # terminals tmux supports.
161	            printf '%s\n' "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
162	            ;;
163	    esac
164	}

166	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
167	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
168	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
169	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
170	#
171	# Smart argument handling:
172	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
173	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
174	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
175	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
176	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
177	function sesh-here() {
178	    local cmd="" target=""
179	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
180	        case "$1" in
181	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
182	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
183	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
184	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
185	        esac
186	    done
187	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
188	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
189	    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
190	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
191	    else
192	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
193	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
194	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
195	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
196	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
197	        local session
198	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
199	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
200	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
201	    fi
202	}
203	
204	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
205	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
206	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
207	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
208	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
209	function sesh-root() {
210	    local cmd="" root
211	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
212	        case "$1" in
213	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
214	            -*)           shift ;;
215	            *)            break ;;
216	        esac
217	    done
218	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
219	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
220	    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
221	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
222	    else
223	        sesh connect "$root"
224	    fi
225	}
226	
227	alias shere='sesh-here'
228	alias sroot='sesh-root'
229	alias scode='sesh-code'
230	alias svibe='sesh-vibe'

232	# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
233	#
234	# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
235	# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
236	# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
237	#
238	# Session naming:
239	#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
240	#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
241	#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
242	#
243	# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
244	# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
245	#
246	# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
247	# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
248	# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
249	# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
250	#
251	# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
252	# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
253	# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
254	#
255	# Usage:
256	#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
257	#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
258	#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
259	#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
260	#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
261	#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
262	#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
263	function sesh-code() {
264	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
265	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
266	        case "$1" in
267	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
268	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
269	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
270	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
271	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
272	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
273	            --agents)
274	                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
275	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
276	                return 1 ;;
277	            -h|--help)
278	                cat <<'EOF'
279	scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout
280	
281	Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
282	             [--no-attach] [AGENT]
283	
284	Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
285	Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
286	Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).
287	
288	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
289	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
290	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
291	
292	--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
293	(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
294	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
295	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
296	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
297	
298	Examples:
299	  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
300	  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
301	  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
302	  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
303	  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
304	  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
305	EOF
306	                return 0 ;;
307	            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
308	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
309	        esac
310	    done
311	
312	    case "$on_exit" in
313	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
314	        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
315	    esac
316	
317	    # Resolve repo root
318	    local repo_root
319	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
320	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
321	    else
322	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
323	    fi
324	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
325	        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
326	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
331	    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
332	    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
333	    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
334	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
335	        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
336	        return 1
337	    fi
338	
339	    local repo_name session
340	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
341	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")
342	
343	    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
344	    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
345	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
346	        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
347	        return 0
348	    fi
349	
350	    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
351	    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
352	    #
353	    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
354	    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
355	    local agent_inner agent_cmd
356	    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
357	    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")
358	
359	    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
360	    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
361	    # pane/window vanishing.
362	    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
363	    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
364	
365	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
366	    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
367	    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
368	    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
369	    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null
370	
371	    # Monitor window
372	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
373	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
374	    else                                       monitor_inner=top
375	    fi
376	    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
377	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"
378	
379	    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
380	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
381	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"
382	
383	    [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
384	}

386	# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
387	#
388	# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
389	# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
390	# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
391	#
392	# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
393	# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
394	#
395	# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
396	# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
397	# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
398	# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
399	# recoverable.
400	#
401	# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
402	#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
403	#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
404	#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
405	#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
406	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
407	#                                 ambiguity)
408	#
409	# Usage:
410	#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
411	#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
412	#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
413	#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
414	#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
415	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
416	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
417	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
418	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
419	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
420	function sesh-vibe() {
421	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
422	    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
423	    local agent_cli="claude"
424	    local agents_csv=""
425	    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
426	    # Seconds to wait between launching each agent pane. Default 0.25s staggers
427	    # startup so DB-backed agents (opencode opens a single global SQLite DB and
428	    # runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`, which needs a brief exclusive lock)
429	    # don't race on a simultaneous cold start. Set 0 to launch all at once.

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** (tmux is Session → Window → Pane). "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
23	
24	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
27	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
28	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
29	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
30	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
31	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
32	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
33	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
34	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
35	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
36	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
37	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
38	
39	## Keybindings
40	
41	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
42	
43	| Key | Action | Type |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
46	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
47	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
48	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
49	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
50	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
51	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
52	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
53	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
54	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
55	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
56	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
57	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
58	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
59	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
60	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
61	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
62	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
63	
64	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
65	
66	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
67	
68	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
69	
70	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
71	
72	```bash
73	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
74	```
75	
76	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
77	
78	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
79	
80	## Television integration
81	
82	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
83	
84	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
85	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
86	
87	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
88	
89	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
90	
91	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
92	
93	```bash
94	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
95	```
96	
97	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
98	
99	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
100	
101	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
102	
103	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
106	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
107	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
108	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
109	
110	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
111	
112	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
113	
114	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
115	
116	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
117	
118	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
119	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
120	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
121	
122	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
123	
124	## See also
125	
126	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
127	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
128
```

1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator.
2	#
3	# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
4	# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other, never
5	# nested. Nothing here touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.
6	#
7	# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
8	# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
9	# Full feasibility matrix + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
10	#
11	# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
12	# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
13	#
14	# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
15	# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
16	# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
17	# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
18	# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.
19	
20	[theme]
21	name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
22	auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
23	light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
24	dark_name = "catppuccin"
25	
26	[ui]
27	mouse_capture = true
28	pane_borders = true
29	pane_gaps = true
30	confirm_close = true
31	show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
32	
33	[terminal]
34	shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
35	new_cwd = "follow"            # new panes inherit the focused pane's cwd
36	
37	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
38	# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
39	# not listed here.
40	[keys]
41	split_vertical = "prefix+|"        # side-by-side, like tmux prefix+|
42	split_horizontal = "prefix+minus"  # stacked, like tmux prefix+- (also the default)
43	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
44	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
45	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
46	
47	# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
48	# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
49	# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
50	# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
51	# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.
52	
53	[[keys.command]]
54	key = "prefix+G"
55	type = "pane"
56	command = "lazygit"
57	description = "lazygit (popup pane)"
58	
59	[[keys.command]]
60	key = "prefix+`"
61	type = "pane"
62	command = "$SHELL"
63	description = "scratch shell (popup pane)"
64	
65	[[keys.command]]
66	key = "prefix+U"
67	type = "pane"
68	command = "tv tools"
69	description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"
70	
71	[[keys.command]]
72	key = "prefix+T"
73	type = "pane"
74	command = "tv herdr-sesh"
75	description = "Session / workspace / dir switcher (herdr-aware tv channel)"
76	
77	[[keys.command]]
78	key = "prefix+a"
79	type = "pane"
80	command = "tv herdr-agent-panes"
81	description = "Live agent panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"
82	
83	[[keys.command]]
84	key = "prefix+f"
85	type = "pane"
86	command = "tv fleet-hosts"
87	description = "Fleet hosts SSH picker (tv)"
88	
89	# --- herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + popup-menu analog) ---
90	# Requires: herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus
91	# Projects = declarative multi-pane workspace templates (see
92	# dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/).
93	# Quick Actions = fuzzy command launcher. If the plugin is not installed these
94	# bindings simply no-op.
95	
96	[[keys.command]]

101

103	key = "prefix+y"

## 1. `sesh-vibe` / `svibe` — the parametric multi-agent layout

Header/doc comment: lines **386–419**. Function body: lines **420–696**. Alias `svibe='sesh-vibe'` at line **230**.

### Defaults (420–431)
```
local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
local agent_cli="claude"
local agents_csv=""
local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"          # line 425
local launch_stagger="${SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"  # line 431
```
- Default agent is `claude`; default pane count starts at 4 but is overridden by auto-pick unless the user passes N.
- `min_width` default 80, overridable by `$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` or `--min-width`.
- `launch_stagger` default 0.25s, overridable by `$SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`; staggers pane launches so DB-backed agents (opencode's global SQLite + WAL pragma) don't race on cold start.

### Argument parsing (432–501)
Flags: `-p|--path`, `--on-exit`, `--agents`, `--min-width`, `--no-specstory` (sets `specstory_mode=never`), `--specstory` (sets `auto`), `--no-attach`, `-h|--help` (heredoc), unknown `-*` → error, `*` → `break` (positional handling happens after the loop). Then integer validation for `min_width` (503–506) and numeric validation for `launch_stagger` (510–513).

### Terminal width source (519)
```
local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
```
`$COLUMNS` first (both shells maintain it on SIGWINCH), `tput cols` fallback, `200` last resort.

### Building the agents array — two mutually exclusive modes (525–570)
- **Heterogeneous** (`--agents` CSV, 527–546): rejects mixing with positional args (528–531); parses CSV portably via `printf … | tr ',' '\n'` piped into `while IFS= read -r tok` with single leading/trailing space trim (536–542); errors if empty. **List length = pane count.**
- **Homogeneous** (positional `[N] [CLI]`, 547–570): if `$1` matches `^[0-9]+$` it becomes `n_agents` and sets `n_agents_set=1` (550–552); next positional becomes `agent_cli` (554). Then the **auto-pick-N block (559–563)** — this is the `min_width` logic you asked about:
```
if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
    n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
    (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
    (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
fi
```
i.e. **N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12)** only when the user did not pass an explicit count. Then a homogeneous array of length `n_agents` is built (566–569).

After both paths: `--on-exit` value is validated to `shell|kill|restart` (572–575), and the final agent count is range-checked to `[1,12]` (577–580).

### Git-repo requirement + session naming (582–621)
Repo root resolved from `--path` (via `cd … && _sesh_git_root`) or CWD (582–588). **Refuses outside a git repo** (589–593: "svibe: not inside a git repo… Use `shere`"). Then fail-fast CLI validation with de-dup (598–617, uses `local -A seen` — the bash-4 requirement), printing missing agents and an "Available:" list scanned from `claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini` (612). Session name (619–621):
```
repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
```
So the name is **`vibe/<repo-basename>`**, sanitized. Idempotent: if the session already exists it just attaches (624–627).

### Layout construction — how it splits panes and sets the window layout (633–695)
A nested helper composes each pane's command (633–637):
```
_vibe_agent_cmd() {
    local inner
    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
}
```
Window 1 (`agents`) is created with the first pane (644–646):
```
local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
    "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "$first_agent")"
```
**Columns-vs-tiled decision (652–659)** — the second use of `min_width`:
```
local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
(( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
local svibe_layout
if (( ${#agents[@]} <= max_columns )); then
    svibe_layout="even-horizontal"     # columns
else
    svibe_layout="tiled"               # grid
fi
```
So if every pane can be ≥ `min_width` cols wide side-by-side → `even-horizontal` (columns); otherwise `tiled`. Remaining panes are added in a loop with the stagger sleep and a re-balance after each split (662–671):

        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "$a")"
    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null

```
Then `unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd` (673). Window 2 `git` = lazygit (on-exit-wrapped) if present, else `git status; exec $SHELL` (678–685). Window 3 `edit` = on-exit-wrapped `nvim` (687–689). Focus set to `agents` window, pane 1 (692–693), then attach unless `--no-attach` (695).

## 2. Helper functions svibe relies on — and herdr-reusability

Defined under the "Internal helpers" banner (line 50 onward). For each I note **PURE (shell-agnostic, reusable by a herdr variant that shells out to a herdr CLI)** vs **TMUX-SPECIFIC**.

| Helper | Lines | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_sesh_git_root` | 57–59 | **PURE** | Just `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Fully reusable. |
| `_sesh_sanitize` | 63–65 | **PURE** | `printf '%s\n' "${1//[.:[:space:]]/-}"`. String-only. Motivated by tmux name rules but has no tmux dependency — reusable (herdr would want the same sanitization for session ids). |
| `_sesh_attach_or_switch` | 69–76 | **TMUX-SPECIFIC** | `tmux switch-client` vs `tmux attach-session` based on `$TMUX`. A herdr variant would replace this with its own attach/connect call. |
| `_sesh_ensure_session` | 81–88 | **TMUX-SPECIFIC** | `tmux has-session` / `tmux new-session`. Return code (0=existed, 1=created) is the reusable *contract*, but the body is tmux. |
| `_sesh_wrap_agent` (the specstory-wrapping helper) | 101–124 | **PURE** | This *is* the specstory wrapper — there is no separate specstory helper. Takes `$1=agent`, `$2=mode(auto\|never)`. `never` → prints `${agent:-claude}` raw (107). `auto` → `case` (110–123): empty/`specstory` → `specstory run`; **known providers `claude\|codex\|cursor\|droid\|gemini` → `specstory run $agent` (115)**; anything else (e.g. `opencode`) → raw passthrough. Pure string transformation, fully reusable. |
| `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (the `--on-exit shell/kill/restart` machinery) | 139–164 | **PURE (command-string builder)** | Builds a **shell** command string, not a tmux call. `guard="trap '' INT;"` (149) so the wrapper ignores Ctrl+C while the inner cmd handles it. `kill` → inner unchanged (151–153); `restart` → `while true; do $inner \|\| true; …; sleep 1; done; exec $SHELL -l` (154–157); `shell` (default) → runs inner, prints a yellow re-run hint, then `exec $SHELL -l` (158–162). The rationale is tmux-motivated ("pane vanishes"), but the output is a plain shell string — a herdr variant that runs a shell command per agent could reuse it verbatim. |
| `_vibe_agent_cmd` (nested inside svibe) | 633–637 | **PURE** | Pure composition of `_sesh_wrap_agent` + `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`. Reusable. |
| Agent-CLI detection / known-provider list | 598–617 (svibe), 334–337 (scode), 612 & 115 | **PURE** | Detection is `command -v "$a"`. Two provider lists exist: the specstory-wrap case list `claude\|codex\|cursor\|droid\|gemini` (115) and the "Available:" advisory scan `claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini` (612). Both pure logic. |

**Summary for a herdr port:** everything that decides *what command to run* is pure and reusable — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent`, `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`, `_vibe_agent_cmd`, the auto-pick-N math, the columns/tiled math, and CLI detection. Only the two functions that *talk to tmux* — `_sesh_attach_or_switch` and `_sesh_ensure_session` — plus the inline `tmux new-session/split-window/select-layout/new-window/select-window/select-pane` calls in the layout builders (645–693) are tmux-specific and would need swapping for herdr CLI calls.

## 3. Sibling functions for comparison

### `sesh-code` / `scode` (263–384; alias line 229; doc 232–262)
Closest sibling to svibe. **Shares:** `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent`, `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`, `_sesh_attach_or_switch`; the `--on-exit shell/kill/restart` machinery (validated 312–315); `--specstory`/`--no-specstory`; `--no-attach`; **git-repo requirement** (324–328, refuses with a hint to use shere/svibe); **per-repo session naming** `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (341); idempotent attach (345–348); single-agent CLI validation (334–337). **Differs:** single agent only (explicitly rejects `--agents`, 273–276); fixed layout built directly with tmux — window `editor` = `nvim` (on-exit-wrapped) left + wrapped agent right, `main-vertical` then `resize-pane … -x 75%` (365–369), plus a `monitor` window running `btop`→`htop`→`top` fallback (372–377). No parametric pane count, no `min_width`/stagger logic.

### `sesh-here` / `shere` (177–202; alias 227; doc 166–176)
Lightweight, **no layout, no git requirement**. Smart arg handling: `-c|--command`, `-p|--path`, bare trailing args become the command (179–188). With a command → `sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"` (190). Without → bypasses sesh's `startup_command` by building a plain shell session directly: `_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")"` → `_sesh_ensure_session` → `_sesh_attach_or_switch` (198–200). Shares only the sanitize/ensure/attach helpers with svibe.

### `sesh-root` / `sroot` (209–225; alias 228; doc 204–208)
Resolves git root else `$PWD` (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel … || root=$PWD`, 219). Same smart `-c`/bare-command handling. Delegates to plain `sesh connect [--command] "$root"` (220–224) — **does not build a layout and does not use the tmux helpers directly**; it leans on sesh's own connect + startup_command. Shares the command-parsing pattern and git-root idea, not the layout machinery.

Common thread across all four: `-p/--path` path resolution, `sesh connect`/tmux session model, and (for scode/svibe) the same helper stack + git-repo gating + collision-safe `<kind>/<repo>` session naming.

For contrast, the repo *does* ship dedicated `compdef` completion files for other in-house CLIs (`_fleet`, `_mlf`, `_pqsum`, `_x`, `_ping_monitor`, `_dotcfg`, `_agent_warmup`, `wt`) under `dot_config/zsh/tools/*_completion.zsh` — so a herdr/svibe completion would be a net-new addition following that established pattern. The only other mentions of svibe/scode elsewhere are prose comments (`41_github.sh:48`, `43_copilot_proxy.sh:295`, `23_mrun.zsh:16`), not completions.

---

### One portability caveat worth flagging for a herdr port
`svibe` de-dups agent names with `local -A seen` (line 600), which requires **bash 4+** (fails on macOS system bash 3.2 at call time — noted at lines 17–18). `_vibe_agent_cmd` uses `"${agents[@]:0:1}"` / `"${agents[@]:1}"` array slicing (644, 662) specifically chosen to work identically in bash and zsh, sidestepping the bash-0-indexed / zsh-1-indexed fork (comment 641–643). Any herdr variant reusing this logic inherits the bash-4 floor.

 `https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar`

```text
Short answer
- What it is: CodexBar is a macOS menu‑bar app to show “every AI coding limit” and provider reset/usage info.  
  Quote: "Every AI coding limit, in your menu bar."
- Data sources: on‑device reuse of provider sessions and local files plus API/OAuth where available. It does not crawl the whole disk; it "reads a small set of known locations (browser cookies/local storage, provider config files, local JSONL logs)." (quote)

Config & files it reads
- Config paths: ~/.config/codexbar/config.json (new installs) and legacy ~/.codexbar/config.json. (quoted paths shown as exact)
- CLI/credential files referenced: ~/.codex and ~/.claude (used by CLI/OAuth fallbacks).
- Browser data / Keychain: reads browser cookies/localStorage when enabled; may decrypt Chromium "Safe Storage" via Keychain (described in Keychain section).

How it obtains usage/rate-limit data (summary by provider)
- Codex — via OAuth API or a local Codex CLI; optional OpenAI web dashboard enrichments.
- OpenAI — Admin API key (usage/cost graphs); falls back to legacy credit-balance if needed.
- Claude — OAuth API, browser cookies, or CLI PTY fallback; session and weekly usage where available.
- Cursor — browser session cookies for plan, usage and billing resets.
- OpenCode / OpenCode Go — browser cookies or local SQLite for workspace/Go usage.
- Gemini — OAuth-backed quota API using Gemini CLI credentials (no browser cookies).
- Copilot — GitHub device flow + Copilot internal usage API.
- Grok — Grok CLI billing RPC with grok.com browser-session fallback.
- GroqCloud — API key for Prometheus-style request/token/cache metrics.
- ElevenLabs — API key for character credits and voice slot usage.
- Deepgram — API key usage summaries across speech/agent/token/TTS.
- z.ai, MiniMax, Kiro, Kilo, Kiro, Kiro/others — mix of API tokens, cookie headers, browser cookies, or CLI auth (each provider line in docs states which).
- Vertex AI — gcloud OAuth with token cost tracking (uses local Claude logs for cost where available).
- AWS Bedrock — AWS access keys / named profile (SSO/assume-role) for Cost Explorer spend and optional CloudWatch Claude activity.
- OpenRouter, LiteLLM, LLM Proxy, Codebuff, Command Code, etc. — API token/key + base/proxy URL or browser cookies depending on provider; many expose credit or quota endpoints and CodexBar parses them or uses local CLI outputs.
- Local-only probes (experimental): Antigravity — local language server probe; no external auth.

Sources of auth / session reuse (methods)
- OAuth / device flow where providers support it.
- Reusing existing browser sessions (cookies/localStorage) when the user opts in.
- API keys stored in CodexBar config (settable from CLI).
- Local CLIs and config files (Codex/Claude CLIs, gcloud, provider CLIs).
- Local JSONL logs and local SQLite caches where providers write usage.

Quoted file/path mentions (exact)
- "~/.config/codexbar/config.json"
- "~/.codexbar/config.json"
- "~/.codex" and "~/.claude"
- "reads a small set of known locations (browser cookies/local storage, provider config files, local JSONL logs)."

Notes / privacy
- The app is privacy-first: it "reuses existing provider sessions — OAuth, device flow, API keys, browser cookies, local files" so it does not store passwords and only reads the small set of known locations when features are enabled.

If you want, I can extract the exact per-provider acquisition line for any specific provider from the README.

## 3. Sibling functions for comparison

### `sesh-code` / `scode` (263–384; alias line 229; doc 232–262)
Closest sibling to svibe. **Shares:** `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent`, `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`, `_sesh_attach_or_switch`; the `--on-exit shell/kill/restart` machinery (validated 312–315); `--specstory`/`--no-specstory`; `--no-attach`; **git-repo requirement** (324–328, refuses with a hint to use shere/svibe); **per-repo session naming** `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (341); idempotent attach (345–348); single-agent CLI validation (334–337). **Differs:** single agent only (explicitly rejects `--agents`, 273–276); fixed layout built directly with tmux — window `editor` = `nvim` (on-exit-wrapped) left + wrapped agent right, `main-vertical` then `resize-pane … -x 75%` (365–369), plus a `monitor` window running `btop`→`htop`→`top` fallback (372–377). No parametric pane count, no `min_width`/stagger logic.

### `sesh-here` / `shere` (177–202; alias 227; doc 166–176)
Lightweight, **no layout, no git requirement**. Smart arg handling: `-c|--command`, `-p|--path`, bare trailing args become the command (179–188). With a command → `sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"` (190). Without → bypasses sesh's `startup_command` by building a plain shell session directly: `_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")"` → `_sesh_ensure_session` → `_sesh_attach_or_switch` (198–200). Shares only the sanitize/ensure/attach helpers with svibe.

### `sesh-root` / `sroot` (209–225; alias 228; doc 204–208)
Resolves git root else `$PWD` (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel … || root=$PWD`, 219). Same smart `-c`/bare-command handling. Delegates to plain `sesh connect [--command] "$root"` (220–224) — **does not build a layout and does not use the tmux helpers directly**; it leans on sesh's own connect + startup_command. Shares the command-parsing pattern and git-root idea, not the layout machinery.

Common thread across all four: `-p/--path` path resolution, `sesh connect`/tmux session model, and (for scode/svibe) the same helper stack + git-repo gating + collision-safe `<kind>/<repo>` session naming.

## 3. How the two herdr tv channels dispatch actions

### `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml` (sesh analog)
- Two sources cycled with Ctrl+S (lines 20-24): (1) `herdr workspace list | jq …` → rows tagged `ws`; (2) `zoxide query -l | awk …` → rows tagged `dir`. TSV: col0=kind, col1=ref, col2=display.
- Keybindings (lines 48-50):
  - **Enter → `actions:open`**: dispatches on kind (lines 52-62) — `ws` → `herdr workspace focus "$ref"`; `dir` → `herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus`. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Ctrl-d → `[actions:close_ws, reload_source]`**: for a `ws` row runs `herdr workspace close "$ref"`, then reloads the list (lines 64-70). `mode = "fork"`.
- Preview (lines 28-43): `ws` → `herdr workspace get "$ref" | jq .`; `dir` → `eza -la --git` (fallback `ls -la`).

### `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml` (agent-panes analog)
- Source (line 25): `herdr pane list | jq …` → TSV pane_id, workspace_id, tab_id, agent_status, cwd.
- Keybindings (lines 46-51):
  - **Enter and Alt-t → `actions:focus`** (lines 53-60): since herdr has no focus-pane-by-id, it jumps to the pane's workspace+tab — `herdr workspace focus "$ws"` then `herdr tab focus "$tab"`. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Alt-k → `actions:close_pane`** (lines 62-75): prompts `Close pane %s? [y/N]`, on yes runs `herdr pane close "$p"`. `mode = "execute"`.
  - **Ctrl-y → `actions:copy_id`** (lines 77-88): copies pane_id via pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip/OSC-52. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Alt-p → `actions:copy_dir`** (lines 90-101): copies the cwd (TSV col4) via the same clipboard cascade. `mode = "fork"`.
- Preview (lines 29-38): prints pane/workspace/tab/cwd headers then `herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80`.

Both channels also declare `requirements` (`herdr`, `jq`, plus `zoxide` for herdr-sesh).

## 5. Cross-file maintenance rules that apply when ADDING a herdr shell helper and/or doc page

Source: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/CLAUDE.md`, § "Cross-file maintenance rules" (lines 7-41). The rule is: *when you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.* The ones that would fire:

**If you add a new herdr shell helper (alias/function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`):**
- **Line 16** — Alias / shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` → add a row to `docs/shells/aliases.md` (name, type, source, scope, one-line). Ref: `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md`.
- **Lines 33-41 (Three-tier file placement)** — choose the tier: `dot_config/shell/` (POSIX, both shells), `dot_config/zsh/` (ZLE/compdef/bindkey/setopt), or `dot_config/bash/` (bind -x/ble.sh/OMB). If porting a zsh widget to bash via ble.sh, extract a shared backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's binding in its own dir.
- **Line 23** — only if the helper is a new *in-house CLI* under `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` (or a new subcommand): add tab completion for BOTH shells (`dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`), keep them in sync, add a row to `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` Section F, and (if it ships an `<tool>-update-completion` helper) a row to the aliases.md Package Managers section. A plain alias/function does not trigger this; a new `bin/executable_*` does.
- **Line 26** — if the helper introduces a `Ctrl+`/`Alt+` keybinding: cross-check the namespace (tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+`) and update `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (and the other keybinding docs listed).
- **Line 24** — if the helper is a stable new CLI or is gated on a new prompt key and should be *surfaced to agents*: update `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl` (the per-host templated agent index). Note it re-renders every `chezmoi apply`, so only edit it to name a stable new CLI or gate on a new prompt key — a plain herdr alias would typically NOT need it.

**If you add a new doc page (e.g. expanding herdr docs) or any `docs/**/*.md`:**
- **Line 14** — New `docs/**/*.md` → add a nav entry in `mkdocs.yml` and run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (the existing herdr nav entry is `mkdocs.yml:264`, `- herdr (tmux alternative, trial): tools/herdr.md`). Known anchor-drift is tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md` — don't tighten `validation.links.not_found`.
- **Line 13** — if the change also touches config/ansible/platform/setup: update `README.md` (What You Get / Supported Platforms / Quick Setup).

**If the herdr install mechanism changes (new tool or switched mechanism):**
- **Line 15** — update the A–Z row in `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` § Tool index. The existing herdr rows are `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:1013-1014` (`herdr` = brew/GitHub-release-single-binary → devtools; `herdr-plus` = `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus` → devtools). If the *mechanism* is new, also update the Per-manager catalog subsection and Decision tree, and `docs/this_repo/upgrades.md` if the upgrade story is non-trivial.

**Repo-root exclusion (line 31):** `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md`, `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `NOTES.md` stay OUT of MkDocs nav (referenced via absolute GitHub URLs from `docs/for-maintainers.md`).

Not triggered by a herdr helper, but worth noting for orientation: the **Workmux 6-file status integration** (CLAUDE.md lines 43-54) is a *separate* mechanism — herdr uses native agent detection (`herdr integration install`, `herdr pane report-agent`) and per `docs/tools/herdr.md:97` the workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system is deliberately untouched, so adding herdr support does NOT pull in those 6 files.

## 3. How the two herdr tv channels dispatch actions

### `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml` (sesh analog)
- Two sources cycled with Ctrl+S (lines 20-24): (1) `herdr workspace list | jq …` → rows tagged `ws`; (2) `zoxide query -l | awk …` → rows tagged `dir`. TSV: col0=kind, col1=ref, col2=display.
- Keybindings (lines 48-50):
  - **Enter → `actions:open`**: dispatches on kind (lines 52-62) — `ws` → `herdr workspace focus "$ref"`; `dir` → `herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus`. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Ctrl-d → `[actions:close_ws, reload_source]`**: for a `ws` row runs `herdr workspace close "$ref"`, then reloads the list (lines 64-70). `mode = "fork"`.
- Preview (lines 28-43): `ws` → `herdr workspace get "$ref" | jq .`; `dir` → `eza -la --git` (fallback `ls -la`).

### `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml` (agent-panes analog)
- Source (line 25): `herdr pane list | jq …` → TSV pane_id, workspace_id, tab_id, agent_status, cwd.
- Keybindings (lines 46-51):
  - **Enter and Alt-t → `actions:focus`** (lines 53-60): since herdr has no focus-pane-by-id, it jumps to the pane's workspace+tab — `herdr workspace focus "$ws"` then `herdr tab focus "$tab"`. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Alt-k → `actions:close_pane`** (lines 62-75): prompts `Close pane %s? [y/N]`, on yes runs `herdr pane close "$p"`. `mode = "execute"`.
  - **Ctrl-y → `actions:copy_id`** (lines 77-88): copies pane_id via pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip/OSC-52. `mode = "fork"`.
  - **Alt-p → `actions:copy_dir`** (lines 90-101): copies the cwd (TSV col4) via the same clipboard cascade. `mode = "fork"`.
- Preview (lines 29-38): prints pane/workspace/tab/cwd headers then `herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80`.

Both channels also declare `requirements` (`herdr`, `jq`, plus `zoxide` for herdr-sesh).

Source: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/CLAUDE.md`, § "Cross-file maintenance rules" (lines 7-41). The rule is: *when you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.* The ones that would fire:

**If you add a new herdr shell helper (alias/function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`):**
- **Line 16** — Alias / shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` → add a row to `docs/shells/aliases.md` (name, type, source, scope, one-line). Ref: `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md`.
- **Lines 33-41 (Three-tier file placement)** — choose the tier: `dot_config/shell/` (POSIX, both shells), `dot_config/zsh/` (ZLE/compdef/bindkey/setopt), or `dot_config/bash/` (bind -x/ble.sh/OMB).
