# herdr research report (v0.7.1 on this machine; server 0.7.0)

Top-level: `herdr — terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents`. Config: `/Users/david/.config/herdr/config.toml`. Home: https://herdr.dev, docs https://herdr.dev/docs/, CLI reference https://herdr.dev/docs/cli-reference/. All subcommands are thin wrappers over a unix-socket API that emit newline-delimited JSON.

Transparency note: while probing herdr-plus I ran `herdr-plus projects --help`, which does NOT print help — it fired the plugin's `projects` action and briefly opened a zoomed "Projects" picker pane. It self-closed (subsequent `workspace/tab list` show no leftover pane; nothing was created/killed by me otherwise). No sessions/workspaces/panes were intentionally created, modified, attached, or killed.

## GOAL 1 — Can a shell wrapper build a multi-pane layout like `tmux split-window`/`new-window`? YES for (a)-(d), all via the native CLI.

The native `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` subcommands cover everything. IDs are hierarchical strings and come back in the JSON on every call, so a wrapper captures them with `jq`. Confirmed live: workspace `w4`, tab `w4:t1`, pane `w4:p1`, `terminal_id` `term_...`. Example real output: `{"result":{"workspaces":[{"label":"chezmoi","workspace_id":"w4",...}]}}`.

(a) New workspace/"space" with a working dir — YES
```
herdr workspace create [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus] [--no-focus]
```
Returns the new `workspace_id`. (Its first tab/pane is created with it.)

(b) Create/split N panes, each launching a specific command — YES, two mechanisms:
- Cleanest (command runs directly in a brand-new pane, tmux-like):
```
herdr agent start <name> [--cwd PATH] [--workspace ID] [--tab ID] [--split right|down] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus] -- <argv...>
```
  e.g. `herdr agent start claude --workspace w4 --split right -- claude` ; `... -- codex` ; `... -- opencode`.
- Split-then-run (there is NO `--command` flag on `pane split` or `tab create`; you create the empty pane, capture its `pane_id`, then run):
```
herdr pane split [<pane_id>|--pane ID|--current] --direction right|down [--ratio FLOAT] [--cwd PATH] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]
herdr pane run <pane_id> <command>        # writes command text + Enter atomically
herdr pane send-text <pane_id> <text>     # literal text, NO Enter
```
  Note: `--direction` only accepts `right|down` (no `left|up`); build then reorder with `herdr pane swap`. Resize with `herdr pane resize --direction ... --amount FLOAT`.

(c) A lazygit pane/tab and an nvim pane/tab — YES, same primitives:
```
herdr tab create [--workspace ID] [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]
herdr pane run <new_pane_id> lazygit        # or nvim
```
  or `herdr agent start lazygit --tab <id> --split down -- lazygit`. (lazygit is even the documented example in `config.toml`'s custom-command section.)

(d) Attach/focus the result — YES:
```
herdr workspace focus <workspace_id>
herdr tab focus <tab_id>
herdr pane focus --direction left|right|up|down [--pane ID|--current]
herdr agent focus <target>
herdr session attach <name>                 # attach the whole persistent session; bare `herdr` attaches default
herdr terminal attach <terminal_id> [--takeover]   # direct single-pane attach (detach: ctrl+b q)
```
  Plus `--focus/--no-focus` on every create/split call.

JSON output: `list`/`get`/`worktree`/`session`/`agent explain`/`plugin` commands take `--json`; but the create/split/run socket commands print JSON responses by default (verified: `workspace list` etc. emit JSON with no flag). Wrapper pattern: `ws=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$DIR" --label X | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id')`.

Reference implementation you can copy: herdr-plus itself builds entire workspaces this way. `/Users/david/.config/herdr/plugins/github/cloudmanic.herdr-plus-0cce37b56fb9/herdr.go` opens `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, sends newline-delimited JSON-RPC (`workspace.create`, `tab.create`, pane run), and parses `workspace_id`/`tab_id`/`pane_id` back — exactly what a shell wrapper would do over the CLI.

### herdr-plus "Projects" launched non-interactively? NO (today).
herdr-plus (v0.1.10, installed) Projects are declarative TOML in `~/.config/herdr-plus/projects/*.toml`. Format (from `.../examples/projects/example.toml`):
```toml
name = "Options Cafe"
description = "..."
group = "Cloudmanic"                 # optional heading
working_dir = "~/Development/options-cafe/options.cafe"   # ~ and $VARS expand
[[tabs]]
name = "claude"
command = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --chrome"
[[tabs]]
name = "lazygit"
command = "lazygit"
[[tabs]]                             # a tab can split into up to 4 panes
name = "server"
[[tabs.panes]]
command = "php artisan serve"
[[tabs.panes]]
command = "npm run dev"
split = "down"                       # "down" | "right"
```
But the ONLY launch path is the interactive fuzzy picker. The binary help states: `run its actions through herdr (e.g. herdr plugin action invoke cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects)`. That action opens the zoomed picker UI (`./bin/herdr-plus projects-ui`); the registered actions are only `projects`, `quick-actions`, `ping` (plus `herdr-plus version`). There is NO "launch project <name>" or headless flag. So "generate a temp project TOML and launch it non-interactively" is NOT supported by herdr-plus today. Use the native `workspace/tab/pane/agent start` calls instead — they give you the same result headlessly, and your wrapper can even read a project TOML you author and translate it into those calls.

Also available: `herdr plugin pane open --plugin ID --entrypoint ID [--placement overlay|split|tab|zoomed] [--workspace ID] [--target-pane PANE] [--direction right|down] [--cwd PATH] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]`.

## GOAL 2 — Usage/quota status display inside herdr

(i) Built-in usage/quota/token display? NO. herdr core has no usage/token/rate-limit feature. The 264-line `herdr --default-config` has NO `statusline`/`status_bar`/`footer`/`usage`/`quota`/`token`/`widget` keys. The sidebar shows workspaces/tabs/agents and agent STATE only (idle/working/blocked/unknown); `[ui]` exposes `sidebar_width`/`sidebar_min_width`/`sidebar_max_width` but no status-text field.

(ii) Custom, command-driven status text hook we could drive ourselves? YES — this is the important one. herdr has a per-pane/agent metadata API that pushes arbitrary status TEXT into the sidebar:
```
herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source ID [--agent LABEL] [--custom-status TEXT|--clear-custom-status] \
   [--state-label STATUS=TEXT] [--title TEXT|--clear-title] [--seq N] [--ttl-ms N]
herdr pane report-agent <pane_id> --source ID --agent LABEL --state idle|working|blocked|unknown [--custom-status TEXT]
```
`--custom-status` (with `--ttl-ms` for auto-expiry) is exactly the hook to render e.g. `"78%5h 64%wk"` next to an agent in the sidebar from a background loop. Additionally, `config.toml` supports custom-command keybindings that pop a pane or run detached:
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+alt+u"
type = "pane"        # opens a temporary pane, closes on exit  (type = "shell" = detached background)
command = "codex-usage-watch"
```

(iii) Plugin ecosystem — YES, usage/token/quota plugins exist. The community index is https://herdr.dev/plugins/ (JS-loaded), discoverable via GitHub topic `herdr-plugin`. Relevant ones (`gh search repos --topic herdr-plugin`):
- jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit — https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit — the closest herdr analog to CodexBar's Codex provider. Reads local Codex JSONL at `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (default `~/.codex/sessions`, override `CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR`), finds the newest `rate_limits` event, and publishes a compact `"78%5h 64%wk"` label into the herdr agents sidebar via a background service, plus a refreshing terminal pane (`codex-usage-watch`, `codex-usage --compact`). Explicitly does NOT call any OpenAI API — same on-disk source CodexBar uses for Codex.
- Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard — https://github.com/Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard — live per-agent token/cost TUI dashboard pane + toast on agent "done". Sources: Pi session JSONL (`agent_session.path`) and OpenCode server API (`http://127.0.0.1:4096/session/{id}`) / on-disk fallback. Token/cost, not subscription quota.
- fkiene/llmtrim-herdr — per-pane token-savings badge. astkaasa/herdr-tokscale-dashboard — Tokscale dashboard pane. CodyBontecou/herdr-telemetry-bridge — streams model/trace telemetry out. wyattjoh/herdr-plugin-gh-pr — pushes PR status into the sidebar (a working example of the custom-status sidebar hook).

No single herdr plugin replicates CodexBar's full multi-provider menu-bar view. For Claude/ChatGPT quota specifically there is NO dedicated herdr plugin — only Codex is covered (by herdr-codex-usage-kit).

### What CodexBar is, and whether its data is reusable in herdr
- Repo: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar · site: https://codexbar.app/ · install: Homebrew cask `codexbar`.
- "Every AI coding limit, in your menu bar." Config `~/.config/codexbar/config.json` (legacy `~/.codexbar/config.json`); reads a small set of known locations — provider config files, local JSONL logs, browser cookies/localStorage, Keychain. It references `~/.codex` and `~/.claude`.
- Per provider: Codex = OAuth API or local Codex CLI; Claude = OAuth API / browser cookies / Claude CLI PTY; OpenAI/ChatGPT = Admin API key + web dashboard; plus Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Grok, OpenCode, Bedrock, Vertex, etc. So it is a mix of local-file reads and API/OAuth/cookie calls, not a pure disk reader.
- Judgment: The Codex portion of CodexBar (rate_limits under `~/.codex`) is the SAME local data that herdr-codex-usage-kit already surfaces into herdr's sidebar today — so Codex usage is directly replicable in herdr right now. Claude/ChatGPT quotas in CodexBar come from OAuth/cookies/CLI, which no herdr plugin currently mirrors; but because herdr exposes the `herdr pane report-metadata … --custom-status` hook, a small DIY script (a timer that computes the string however you like — even by reading CodexBar's own cached data, or querying the same sources) can push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%5h"` label into herdr's sidebar without any core changes.

Bottom line for GOAL 2: no built-in usage display, but (1) a real command-driven sidebar status hook exists (`pane report-metadata --custom-status`), and (2) a Codex-usage plugin already uses it with the same local data source as CodexBar. Claude/ChatGPT parity would require a small custom driver script.

Sources: [herdr.dev](https://herdr.dev/) · [CLI reference](https://herdr.dev/docs/cli-reference/) · [herdr plugins index](https://herdr.dev/plugins/) · [herdr-plus repo](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) · [herdrplus.com docs](https://herdrplus.com/docs/examples/) · [herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit) · [herdr-token-dashboard](https://github.com/Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard) · [CodexBar repo](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) · [codexbar.app](https://codexbar.app/) · [CodexBar cask](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/codexbar)

What a Project file contains (exact TOML snippets from the docs)
- Basic metadata: "name = \"My App\""  
- Working directory: "working_dir = \"~/Development/my-app\""  
- Tab with a startup command: "[[tabs]]" and "command = \"claude --dangerously-skip-permissions\""  
- Empty tab (no command): "[[tabs]]" and "name = \"terminal\"   # no command — just an empty shell"

===== manifest toml =====
#
# Date: 2026-06-15
# Author: Spicer Matthews (spicer@cloudmanic.com)
# Copyright: 2026 Cloudmanic Labs, LLC. All rights reserved.
#
# herdr-plugin.toml registers herdr-plus with herdr as a first-class plugin.
# Install it with `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus` (herdr clones this
# repo, runs the [[build]] step below, and registers the entry points), or for
# local development `herdr plugin link .` from a checkout.
#
# This is the plugin-first rebuild. It ships Projects (declarative workspace
# templates you fuzzy-pick) and Quick Actions (a fuzzy launcher for one-off
# scripts), plus a `ping` smoke test that proves the plugin loop end to end.

id = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus"
name = "Herdr Plus"
# Kept in sync with internal/version/version.go by .github/workflows/release.yml.
version = "0.1.10"
min_herdr_version = "0.7.0"
description = "An extension for herdr — a collection of tools that make it better. Projects: fuzzy-pick a declarative template to spin up a whole workspace — every tab, pane, and startup command. Quick Actions: a fuzzy launcher for one-off scripts, run in the directory you launched from."
platforms = ["linux", "macos"]

# Produce the binary at install time. herdr runs this once, after you confirm a
# GitHub install and before registering the plugin. The script prefers a local Go
# toolchain (an exact build of the cloned source) and falls back to downloading
# the latest prebuilt release binary, so installing works with or without Go.
# Either way the result is ./bin/herdr-plus, which the entry points below invoke.
[[build]]
command = ["sh", "scripts/build.sh"]

# projects — the flagship action. Opens a full-screen browser to fuzzy-pick a
# project (a declarative set of tabs/panes from ~/.config/herdr-plus/projects/)
# and spins up its whole herdr workspace. Bind a key to it or run it from herdr's
# action menu — see the README.
[[actions]]
id = "projects"
title = "Herdr Plus: Projects"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "projects"]

# picker — the projects browser as a herdr-managed pane (no throwaway workspace).
# Opened by the projects action via `herdr plugin pane open`; herdr gives it a
# zoomed pane, runs the browser, and tears the pane down when it exits.
[[panes]]
id = "picker"
title = "Herdr Plus: Projects"
placement = "zoomed"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "projects-ui"]

# quick-actions — a fuzzy launcher for one-off actions/scripts (command, select,
# or form), loaded from ~/.config/herdr-plus/quick-actions/ (plus a repo's own
# .herdr-plus/quick-actions/). Commands template against and run in the directory
# you launched from. Bind a key or run it from herdr's action menu.
[[actions]]
id = "quick-actions"
title = "Herdr Plus: Quick Actions"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "quick-actions"]

# quick-actions-picker — the action picker as a herdr-managed overlay pane. The
# quick-actions action opens it (passing the launch context), and herdr restores
# your previous focus when it closes.
[[panes]]
id = "quick-actions-picker"
title = "Quick Actions"
placement = "overlay"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "quick-actions-ui"]

# ping — a smoke-test action that proves the plugin loop end to end: it talks to
# herdr over the socket and prints the focused pane/workspace. Its output is
# captured in `herdr plugin log list --plugin cloudmanic.herdr-plus`.
[[actions]]
id = "ping"
title = "Herdr Plus: ping"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "ping"]

# worktree.created / worktree.opened — herdr fires worktree.created when it
# creates a new git worktree and worktree.opened when it opens an existing one
# into a workspace (e.g. the right-click dialog for a branch that already has a
# worktree). Both hand us a fresh workspace that wants tabs, so we subscribe to
# both — otherwise opening an existing worktree would silently skip the layout.
# The handler looks for a matching layout in ~/.config/herdr-plus/worktrees/ and
# lays its tabs/panes into the workspace. It is a quiet no-op when no layout
# matches, and it skips a workspace that already has tabs (so a layout never
# applies twice even if both events fire). herdr runs this for you — never invoke
# it by hand. Output is captured in the plugin log.
[[events]]
on = "worktree.created"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "on-worktree"]

[[events]]
on = "worktree.opened"
command = ["./bin/herdr-plus", "on-worktree"]

===== herdr-plus --help =====
herdr-plus: a herdr plugin; run its actions through herdr (e.g. `herdr plugin action invoke cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects`) or `herdr-plus version`.

===== herdr.go head (how it talks to herdr) =====
//
// Date: 2026-06-15
// Author: Spicer Matthews (spicer@cloudmanic.com)
// Copyright: 2026 Cloudmanic Labs, LLC. All rights reserved.
//

package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// herdrClient talks to the running herdr instance over its unix domain socket.
// The protocol is newline-delimited JSON: one request object per line, one
// response object per line. Each call opens a short-lived connection, writes a
// single request, and reads a single response. herdr injects HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
// into every plugin command, so this works whenever herdr runs us.
type herdrClient struct {
	socketPath string
}

// newHerdrClient builds a client from the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH environment
// variable. It returns an error when the process is not running inside herdr.
func newHerdrClient() (*herdrClient, error) {
	path := os.Getenv("HERDR_SOCKET_PATH")
	if path == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("HERDR_SOCKET_PATH is not set; are you running inside herdr?")
	}
	return &herdrClient{socketPath: path}, nil
}

// request is one JSON-RPC-style message sent to herdr.
type request struct {
	ID     string         `json:"id"`
	Method string         `json:"method"`
	Params map[string]any `json:"params"`
}

// herdrError carries the code and human message herdr returns on failure.
type herdrError struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

// response is one JSON line returned by herdr. Exactly one of Result or Error
// is populated.
type response struct {
	ID     string          `json:"id"`
	Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
	Error  *herdrError     `json:"error"`
}

// call sends a single request over a fresh connection and decodes the result

## GOAL 1 — Can a shell wrapper build a multi-pane layout like `tmux split-window`/`new-window`? YES for (a)-(d), all via the native CLI.

The native `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` subcommands cover everything. IDs are hierarchical strings and come back in the JSON on every call, so a wrapper captures them with `jq`. Confirmed live: workspace `w4`, tab `w4:t1`, pane `w4:p1`, `terminal_id` `term_...`. Example real output: `{"result":{"workspaces":[{"label":"chezmoi","workspace_id":"w4",...}]}}`.

(a) New workspace/"space" with a working dir — YES
```
herdr workspace create [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus] [--no-focus]
```
Returns the new `workspace_id`. (Its first tab/pane is created with it.)

(b) Create/split N panes, each launching a specific command — YES, two mechanisms:
- Cleanest (command runs directly in a brand-new pane, tmux-like):
```
herdr agent start <name> [--cwd PATH] [--workspace ID] [--tab ID] [--split right|down] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus] -- <argv...>
```
  e.g. `herdr agent start claude --workspace w4 --split right -- claude` ; `... -- codex` ; `... -- opencode`.
- Split-then-run (there is NO `--command` flag on `pane split` or `tab create`; you create the empty pane, capture its `pane_id`, then run):
```
herdr pane split [<pane_id>|--pane ID|--current] --direction right|down [--ratio FLOAT] [--cwd PATH] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]
herdr pane run <pane_id> <command>        # writes command text + Enter atomically
herdr pane send-text <pane_id> <text>     # literal text, NO Enter
```
  Note: `--direction` only accepts `right|down` (no `left|up`); build then reorder with `herdr pane swap`. Resize with `herdr pane resize --direction ... --amount FLOAT`.

(c) A lazygit pane/tab and an nvim pane/tab — YES, same primitives:
```
herdr tab create [--workspace ID] [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]
herdr pane run <new_pane_id> lazygit        # or nvim
```
  or `herdr agent start lazygit --tab <id> --split down -- lazygit`. (lazygit is even the documented example in `config.toml`'s custom-command section.)

(d) Attach/focus the result — YES:
```
herdr workspace focus <workspace_id>
herdr tab focus <tab_id>
herdr pane focus --direction left|right|up|down [--pane ID|--current]
herdr agent focus <target>
herdr session attach <name>                 # attach the whole persistent session; bare `herdr` attaches default
herdr terminal attach <terminal_id> [--takeover]   # direct single-pane attach (detach: ctrl+b q)
```
  Plus `--focus/--no-focus` on every create/split call.

JSON output: `list`/`get`/`worktree`/`session`/`agent explain`/`plugin` commands take `--json`; but the create/split/run socket commands print JSON responses by default (verified: `workspace list` etc. emit JSON with no flag). ### herdr-plus "Projects" launched non-interactively? NO (today).
herdr-plus (v0.1.10, installed) Projects are declarative TOML in `~/.config/herdr-plus/projects/*.toml`. Format (from `.../examples/projects/example.toml`):

[[tabs]]

[[tabs]]
name = "lazygit"

```
But the ONLY launch path is the interactive fuzzy picker. The binary help states: `run its actions through herdr (e.g. herdr plugin action invoke cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects)`. There is NO "launch project <name>" or headless flag. So "generate a temp project TOML and launch it non-interactively" is NOT supported by herdr-plus today. Also available: `herdr plugin pane open --plugin ID --entrypoint ID [--placement overlay|split|tab|zoomed] [--workspace ID] [--target-pane PANE] [--direction right|down] [--cwd PATH] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus|--no-focus]`.

## GOAL 2 — Usage/quota status display inside herdr

(i) Built-in usage/quota/token display? NO. herdr core has no usage/token/rate-limit feature. The 264-line `herdr --default-config` has NO `statusline`/`status_bar`/`footer`/`usage`/`quota`/`token`/`widget` keys. The sidebar shows workspaces/tabs/agents and agent STATE only (idle/working/blocked/unknown); `[ui]` exposes `sidebar_width`/`sidebar_min_width`/`sidebar_max_width` but no status-text field.

(ii) Custom, command-driven status text hook we could drive ourselves? YES — this is the important one. herdr has a per-pane/agent metadata API that pushes arbitrary status TEXT into the sidebar:
```
herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source ID [--agent LABEL] [--custom-status TEXT|--clear-custom-status] \
   [--state-label STATUS=TEXT] [--title TEXT|--clear-title] [--seq N] [--ttl-ms N]
herdr pane report-agent <pane_id> --source ID --agent LABEL --state idle|working|blocked|unknown [--custom-status TEXT]
```
`--custom-status` (with `--ttl-ms` for auto-expiry) is exactly the hook to render e.g. `"78%5h 64%wk"` next to an agent in the sidebar from a background loop. Additionally, `config.toml` supports custom-command keybindings that pop a pane or run detached:
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+alt+u"
type = "pane"        # opens a temporary pane, closes on exit  (type = "shell" = detached background)
command = "codex-usage-watch"
```

- fkiene/llmtrim-herdr — per-pane token-savings badge. astkaasa/herdr-tokscale-dashboard — Tokscale dashboard pane. CodyBontecou/herdr-telemetry-bridge — streams model/trace telemetry out. wyattjoh/herdr-plugin-gh-pr — pushes PR status into the sidebar (a working example of the custom-status sidebar hook).

No single herdr plugin replicates CodexBar's full multi-provider menu-bar view. For Claude/ChatGPT quota specifically there is NO dedicated herdr plugin — only Codex is covered (by herdr-codex-usage-kit).

### What CodexBar is, and whether its data is reusable in herdr
- Repo: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar · site: https://codexbar.app/ · install: Homebrew cask `codexbar`.

I have a comprehensive answer. Here are my findings.

## Short answer
Yes — herdr has a **built-in which-key-style keybinding cheatsheet overlay**, triggered by `prefix+?`. It's not an auto-appearing timeout hint like Neovim's which-key; it's an explicit "show every active binding" overlay. No dedicated which-key *plugin* exists (only static/web cheatsheets and fuzzy command-palette plugins), and DIY is largely unnecessary because the built-in already does it dynamically.

---

## 1. BUILT-IN — YES, it exists

**The `help` action, default-bound to `prefix+?`** (prefix defaults to `ctrl+b`).

From `herdr --default-config`, the `[keys]` section lists it among the prefix-mode actions:
```toml
# Prefix-mode actions
# help = "prefix+?"
# settings = "prefix+s"
# detach = "prefix+q"
...
```
It's a first-class configurable action (you can rebind the `help` key in `config.toml`).

The official keyboard docs confirm what it does (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/website/src/content/docs/keyboard.mdx, rendered at https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/):
> "Press `prefix+?` at any time to see every active binding."

Issue #817 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/817, "Keybinds help overlay wraps when an action is bound to multiple 1..9 ranges") confirms the overlay's structure — it renders a **two-column list: a key column plus a per-binding description/label**, e.g. the "switch tab" row. So it is genuinely which-key-like: keys + human-readable labels for every active binding.

**Important nuance vs Neovim which-key:** herdr's overlay is *explicitly invoked* (you press `prefix` then `?`). It does **not** auto-pop after you press the prefix and pause. I found no config option for an auto/timeout follow-up hint — I checked the entire `[keys]` and `[ui]` sections of `--default-config`; there is no `which_key`, `show_help`, `hints`, `cheatsheet`, or `help_overlay` toggle. The only relevant knob is the `help` keybinding itself. So it's best described as a "show all keys" cheatsheet popup rather than a live follow-up-key hint.

There is no `herdr keys` subcommand (falls through to top-level help) and no CLI-level cheatsheet command; the overlay is an in-app (TUI) feature only.

## 2. PLUGIN ecosystem — no dedicated which-key plugin

`herdr plugin --help` confirms plugins exist and CAN open overlay panes:
```
herdr plugin pane open --plugin ID --entrypoint ID [--placement overlay|split|tab|zoomed] ...
herdr plugin action <list|invoke>
```
So a which-key-style plugin is technically possible (plugins can register overlay panes and actions), but searching `gh search repos --topic herdr-plugin --limit 100` plus keyword searches, **none implements a which-key / follow-up-key hint overlay**. The closest matches:

- **cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet** (https://github.com/cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet) — "Single-page Herdr cheatsheet: keybindings, CLI, and an agent setup prompt. GitHub Pages landing." This is a **static web page**, not an in-app overlay.
- **tmstack-io/herdr-cheatsheet** (https://github.com/tmstack-io/herdr-cheatsheet) — no description; appears empty/placeholder.
- Command-palette plugins (adjacent, but these are fuzzy *action runners*, not keybinding-hint overlays): **JanTvrdik/herdr-command-palette** ("fzf command palette for herdr — fuzzy-pick and run any plugin action"), **alon-z/herdr-command-palette**, **thanhdat77/herdr-picker-plus**.

The herdr.dev/plugins index (https://herdr.dev/plugins/) is JS-rendered ("Loading plugins…") and lists nothing statically; the `herdr-plugin` GitHub topic is the real index, and it has no which-key entry. There is no `herdr plugin search` subcommand — discovery is via the GitHub topic; install is `herdr plugin install <owner>/<repo>`.

## 3. DIY feasibility — possible but mostly redundant

Yes, the `[[keys.command]]` mechanism could bind a key to a cheatsheet script. From `--default-config`:
```toml
# [[keys.command]]
# key = "prefix+alt+g"
# type = "pane"          # opens a temporary pane, closes when the command exits
# command = "lazygit"
```
You could bind e.g. `prefix+alt+?` → `type="pane"` → a script that `cat`s a static cheatsheet. **Two caveats:**

1. **Largely unnecessary** — the built-in `prefix+?` overlay already renders a cheatsheet *dynamically from your actual configured bindings*, which a static script can't stay in sync with.
2. **`type="pane"` opens a tiling split, not a floating popup.** Unlike this repo's tmux `display-popup` menu approach, herdr's custom commands reflow the layout. Issue #785 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785, "floating popup / overlay placement for `[[keys.command]]`") requested exactly the tmux-`display-popup`-style centered float and was **CLOSED / not planned**. (Floating `overlay` placement is available to *plugins* via `herdr plugin pane open --placement overlay`, just not to `[[keys.command]]`.)

## Bottom line
herdr ships a native which-key-equivalent: the `prefix+?` **keybinds help overlay** (`help` action, rebindable in `config.toml`), showing every active binding with labels. It differs from Neovim's which-key only in that it's manually invoked rather than auto-appearing after the prefix. No plugin adds an auto-hint version, and DIY via `[[keys.command]]` would be a static split pane inferior to the built-in.

Sources:
- https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/ · https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/website/src/content/docs/keyboard.mdx
- https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
- https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/817 (help overlay structure)
- https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785 (floating popup for keys.command — not planned)
- https://github.com/cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet
</output>

**run all your coding agents in one terminal. see who's blocked, working, or done at a glance.**

run your agents where they already run; your machine, a server, anywhere you can ssh. each one gets its own real terminal, not an app's imitation of one, so even full-screen TUIs render right. click, drag, and split panes into workspaces and tabs, and watch each agent go blocked, working, done. close the laptop and nothing dies; reattach from another terminal, or from your phone over ssh. one local rust binary, not an app: no gui, no electron, no mac-only wrapper, no account, no telemetry. (if you've used tmux: it's that, rebuilt for agents.)

---

## what you get

- **a real terminal per agent.** you see each agent's own screen, not an app's imitation of one, so even full-screen TUIs render right.
- **agent state at a glance.** the sidebar rolls every agent up to 🔴 blocked, 🟡 working, 🔵 done, or 🟢 idle, so you always know who needs you. zero config, no hooks required.
- **workspaces, tabs, panes.** organize by repo or folder, click, drag, and split, mouse-native throughout.
- **nothing dies on detach.** a background server keeps panes and agents alive; detach and reattach from any terminal, including your phone over ssh.
- **runs anywhere.** single ~10MB rust binary, linux and macos (windows beta), no dependencies, runs inside the terminal you already use.
- **scriptable.** a local socket api and cli that agents can drive, plus plugins you can write in any language.

title:	Keybinds help overlay wraps when an action is bound to multiple 1..9 ranges
state:	CLOSED

### Is this a reproducible bug?

- [x] I confirm this is a reproducible bug, not a feature request, idea, question, contribution proposal, or direction check.

### Current behavior

When an index action (e.g. `switch_tab`) is bound to two `1..9` ranges, the keybinds help overlay (`prefix+?`) renders broken: that row expands to all 18 individual bindings (`prefix+1 / prefix+2 / … / alt+9`), making the key column ~180 columns wide, so every other row pads to that width and wraps each description onto its own indented line. Unreadable even in a wide terminal.

### Expected behavior

Each contiguous `1..9` range compacts to `<prefix>1..9`, so two ranges read as `prefix+1..9 / alt+1..9` (like a single range already does). The key column stays narrow and every description stays on one line.

### Reproduction

1. In `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`:

   ```toml
   [keys]
   switch_tab = ["prefix+1..9", "alt+1..9"]
   ```

2. Start herdr and open the keybinds overlay (`prefix+?`).
3. The "switch tab" row shows all 18 bindings expanded and every label in the overlay wraps onto its own indented line.

## Summary

Allow user keybind commands (`[[keys.command]]`) to open in a floating popup / overlay
window instead of only a tiling split pane (`type = "pane"`). This is the primitive
needed for transient, sessionx-style fuzzy pickers (workspace / tab / agent switchers,
scratch shells, lazygit) that should float over the layout rather than reflow it.

## Motivation

I'm porting a tmux workflow to herdr. `tmux-sessionx` runs `fzf` inside a tmux
`display-popup` — a centered floating window that leaves the underlying layout
untouched. I rebuilt it on herdr as a `[[keys.command]]` with `type = "pane"` running an
fzf script that calls `herdr workspace list` / `herdr pane read --format ansi` (live
preview) / `herdr workspace focus`. It works really well — but `type = "pane"` opens a
**tiling split**, so invoking the picker reflows the current layout and then tears the
split back down on exit. Heavier than a popup, and it briefly disturbs the surrounding
panes.

From #701 it looks like plugin panes already support placements such as `overlay` /

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-03 09:13:36Z)**_

I have a comprehensive answer. Here are my findings.

## Short answer
Yes — herdr has a **built-in which-key-style keybinding cheatsheet overlay**, triggered by `prefix+?`. It's not an auto-appearing timeout hint like Neovim's which-key; it's an explicit "show every active binding" overlay. No dedicated which-key *plugin* exists (only static/web cheatsheets and fuzzy command-palette plugins), and DIY is largely unnecessary because the built-in already does it dynamically.

---

## 1. BUILT-IN — YES, it exists

**The `help` action, default-bound to `prefix+?`** (prefix defaults to `ctrl+b`).

From `herdr --default-config`, the `[keys]` section lists it among the prefix-mode actions:
```toml
# Prefix-mode actions
# help = "prefix+?"
# settings = "prefix+s"
# detach = "prefix+q"
...
```
It's a first-class configurable action (you can rebind the `help` key in `config.toml`).

The official keyboard docs confirm what it does (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/website/src/content/docs/keyboard.mdx, rendered at https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/):
> "Press `prefix+?` at any time to see every active binding."

Issue #817 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/817, "Keybinds help overlay wraps when an action is bound to multiple 1..9 ranges") confirms the overlay's structure — it renders a **two-column list: a key column plus a per-binding description/label**, e.g. the "switch tab" row. So it is genuinely which-key-like: keys + human-readable labels for every active binding.

**Important nuance vs Neovim which-key:** herdr's overlay is *explicitly invoked* (you press `prefix` then `?`). It does **not** auto-pop after you press the prefix and pause. I found no config option for an auto/timeout follow-up hint — I checked the entire `[keys]` and `[ui]` sections of `--default-config`; there is no `which_key`, `show_help`, `hints`, `cheatsheet`, or `help_overlay` toggle. The only relevant knob is the `help` keybinding itself. So it's best described as a "show all keys" cheatsheet popup rather than a live follow-up-key hint.

There is no `herdr keys` subcommand (falls through to top-level help) and no CLI-level cheatsheet command; the overlay is an in-app (TUI) feature only.

## 2. PLUGIN ecosystem — no dedicated which-key plugin

`herdr plugin --help` confirms plugins exist and CAN open overlay panes:
```
herdr plugin pane open --plugin ID --entrypoint ID [--placement overlay|split|tab|zoomed] ...
herdr plugin action <list|invoke>
```
So a which-key-style plugin is technically possible (plugins can register overlay panes and actions), but searching `gh search repos --topic herdr-plugin --limit 100` plus keyword searches, **none implements a which-key / follow-up-key hint overlay**. The closest matches:

- **cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet** (https://github.com/cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet) — "Single-page Herdr cheatsheet: keybindings, CLI, and an agent setup prompt. GitHub Pages landing." This is a **static web page**, not an in-app overlay.
- **tmstack-io/herdr-cheatsheet** (https://github.com/tmstack-io/herdr-cheatsheet) — no description; appears empty/placeholder.
- Command-palette plugins (adjacent, but these are fuzzy *action runners*, not keybinding-hint overlays): **JanTvrdik/herdr-command-palette** ("fzf command palette for herdr — fuzzy-pick and run any plugin action"), **alon-z/herdr-command-palette**, **thanhdat77/herdr-picker-plus**.

The herdr.dev/plugins index (https://herdr.dev/plugins/) is JS-rendered ("Loading plugins…") and lists nothing statically; the `herdr-plugin` GitHub topic is the real index, and it has no which-key entry. There is no `herdr plugin search` subcommand — discovery is via the GitHub topic; install is `herdr plugin install <owner>/<repo>`.

## 3. DIY feasibility — possible but mostly redundant

Yes, the `[[keys.command]]` mechanism could bind a key to a cheatsheet script. From `--default-config`:
```toml
# [[keys.command]]
# key = "prefix+alt+g"
# type = "pane"          # opens a temporary pane, closes when the command exits
# command = "lazygit"
```
You could bind e.g. `prefix+alt+?` → `type="pane"` → a script that `cat`s a static cheatsheet. **Two caveats:**

1. **Largely unnecessary** — the built-in `prefix+?` overlay already renders a cheatsheet *dynamically from your actual configured bindings*, which a static script can't stay in sync with.
2. **`type="pane"` opens a tiling split, not a floating popup.** Unlike this repo's tmux `display-popup` menu approach, herdr's custom commands reflow the layout. Issue #785 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785, "floating popup / overlay placement for `[[keys.command]]`") requested exactly the tmux-`display-popup`-style centered float and was **CLOSED / not planned**. (Floating `overlay` placement is available to *plugins* via `herdr plugin pane open --placement overlay`, just not to `[[keys.command]]`.)

## Bottom line
herdr ships a native which-key-equivalent: the `prefix+?` **keybinds help overlay** (`help` action, rebindable in `config.toml`), showing every active binding with labels. It differs from Neovim's which-key only in that it's manually invoked rather than auto-appearing after the prefix. No plugin adds an auto-hint version, and DIY via `[[keys.command]]` would be a static split pane inferior to the built-in.

Sources:
- https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/ · https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/website/src/content/docs/keyboard.mdx
- https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
- https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/817 (help overlay structure)
- https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785 (floating popup for keys.command — not planned)
- https://github.com/cskwork/herdr-cheatsheet

105	        # sensible default (we choose `claude` upstream when --no-specstory
106	        # is set, since `specstory run` with no arg defaults to claude too).
107	        printf '%s\n' "${agent:-claude}"
108	        return
109	    fi
110	    case "$agent" in
111	        ""|"specstory")
112	            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
113	            printf '%s\n' "specstory run"
114	            ;;
115	        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
116	            printf '%s\n' "specstory run $agent"
117	            ;;
118	        *)
119	            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
120	            # later as specstory adds support).
121	            printf '%s\n' "$agent"
122	            ;;
123	    esac
124	}
125	
126	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
127	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
128	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
129	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
130	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
131	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
132	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
133	#             land in shell.
134	#
135	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
136	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
137	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
138	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
139	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
140	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
141	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
142	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
143	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
144	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
145	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
146	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
147	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
148	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
149	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
150	    case "$mode" in
151	        kill)
152	            printf '%s\n' "$inner"
153	            ;;
154	        restart)
155	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
156	            printf '%s\n' "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
157	            ;;
158	        shell|*)
159	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
160	            # terminals tmux supports.
161	            printf '%s\n' "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
162	            ;;
163	    esac
164	}
165	
166	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
167	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
168	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
169	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
170	#
171	# Smart argument handling:
172	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
173	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
174	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
175	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
176	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
177	function sesh-here() {
178	    local cmd="" target=""
179	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
180	        case "$1" in
181	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
182	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
183	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
184	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
185	        esac
186	    done
187	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
188	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
189	    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
190	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
191	    else
192	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
193	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
194	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
195	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
196	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
197	        local session
198	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
199	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
200	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
201	    fi
202	}
203	
204	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
205	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
206	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
207	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
208	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
209	function sesh-root() {
210	    local cmd="" root
211	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
212	        case "$1" in
213	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
214	            -*)           shift ;;

# Plan: `hvibe` / `hcode` — herdr equivalents of `svibe` / `scode` (+ which-key & usage findings)

## Context

Today the repo has rich **tmux** helpers for spinning up a whole coding session in one motion — `svibe` (N agent panes + lazygit + nvim) and `scode` (nvim ‖ one agent + btop), both in `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh`. herdr (the trial tmux-alternative) has **no shell helper at all**: to start work you `cd` into a project, manually `herdr workspace create`, then open each agent CLI / lazygit / nvim by hand. The user wants the same "open the whole pack" one-liner under herdr.

Research (herdr v0.7.1, installed) confirmed this is fully buildable on herdr's native CLI, and that svibe's *pure* logic (specstory-wrap, on-exit-wrap, git-root, agent-CLI detection, auto-N width math) is reusable verbatim — only the `tmux …` calls get swapped for `herdr …` calls. Two side questions were also answered:

- **which-key**: herdr already ships it — `prefix+?` opens a dynamic "all active bindings" overlay (`help` action). Nothing to build; document it.
- **CodexBar-style usage**: herdr has **no** native usage display; a plugin (`jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit`) covers **Codex-only**. Per user decision we will **not install** it now and instead **backlog** a DIY driver (using herdr's `pane report-metadata --custom-status` hook) that could show Claude+Codex parity later.

**User decisions:** build **both** `hvibe` and `hcode`; default layout = **one `agents` tab + side-by-side splits** (svibe parity) with a `--tab-per-agent` opt-in; **backlog** the usage driver. User flagged one thing to verify: *with multiple agents in a single tab, does herdr's bottom-left agent panel show one entry or several?* — if it collapses to one, that's the argument for `--tab-per-agent`.

### 1. New shell backend: `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (shared tier)

5. `edit` tab: same with `nvim`.

# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
#
# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
#
# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
#
# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
#
# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).

# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
        | head -1
}

# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
    local inner
    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
}

# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
function _herdr_tool_tab() {
    local pane
    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
#
# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
#
# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
#
# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
#
# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
#
# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
# has no even-out-splits command.
#
# Usage:
#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
function herdr-vibe() {
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }

    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"

    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
            -h|--help)
                cat <<'EOF'
hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)

Usage:
  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]

Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
  tab "edit"   — nvim
Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).

Two modes for choosing agents:
  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)

Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough

--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
  kill            — let the pane close
  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop

--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.

Examples:
  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
EOF
                return 0 ;;
            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
            *)               break ;;
        esac
    done

    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"

    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
    local -a agents
    agents=()
    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
            return 1
        fi
        local tok
        while IFS= read -r tok; do
            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
            return 1
        fi
    else
        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
        fi
        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
        # --tab-per-agent for more).
        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
        fi
        local k
        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
    fi

    case "$on_exit" in
        shell|kill|restart) ;;
        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac

    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe).
    local repo_root
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
    else
        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
    fi
    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
    local a missing=""
    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
    done
    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local repo label
    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")

    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
    local existing
    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return 0
    fi

    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
    local ws_json ws p0 t0
    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
        done
    else
        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
        local prev="$p0" np
        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
                prev="$np"
            fi
        done
    fi

    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
    local git_inner git_label
    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"

    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
}

# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
#
# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
#
# Usage:
#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
#   hcode --no-specstory claude
#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
function herdr-code() {
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }

    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
            --agents)

                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2

hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)

Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
             [--no-attach] [AGENT]

Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.

Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough

--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart

Examples:
  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
  hcode --on-exit kill claude
EOF
                return 0 ;;
            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
        esac
    done

    case "$on_exit" in
        shell|kill|restart) ;;
        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac

    local repo_root
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
    else
        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
    fi
    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
        return 1
    fi

        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
        return 1

    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")

    local existing

    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then

        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return 0
    fi

    local ws_json ws p0 t0
    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')

    fi

```md
# herdr usage-status driver — CodexBar-analog AI quota in the herdr sidebar

**Status**: P? — researched, not spiked yet (deliberately deferred 2026-07)
**Effort**: M (DIY driver, Codex+Claude) / S (just install the Codex-only plugin)
**Related**: [docs/tools/herdr.md](../docs/tools/herdr.md), `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (`hvibe`/`hcode`), `dot_config/shell/40_codexbar` (existing CodexBar shell aliases `cbu`/`cbc`/`cbca`), [steipete/CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) (brew cask `codexbar`, already installed)

## Context

herdr's sidebar shows per-pane agent **state** (idle / working / blocked) natively but has **no usage / quota / token display** — confirmed against `herdr --default-config` (v0.7.1): no `statusline` / `status_bar` / `usage` / `quota` / `widget` keys; `[ui]` only exposes `sidebar_*_width`. The user already runs **CodexBar** (macOS menu bar, multi-provider: Codex + Claude + ChatGPT + …) as the usage view, wired into the shell via `40_codexbar` (`cbu`/`cbc`/`cbca`). The question was whether the same "% used" info can live **inside herdr** next to the agents.

Decision at research time: **keep CodexBar as the primary usage view; do not install a herdr plugin now.** Backlog a DIY driver for when the user lives in herdr full-time and wants Claude+Codex quota in the sidebar without alt-tabbing to the menu bar.

## The hook (verified)

herdr can render arbitrary status TEXT next to a pane/agent in the sidebar via the metadata API:

\```
herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source <id> --custom-status "Claude 62% • Codex 78%5h" --ttl-ms <n>
\```

`--custom-status` + `--ttl-ms` (auto-expiry) is exactly the driver surface — a background timer computes the string and pushes it per pane. (`herdr pane report-agent … --custom-status` is the other entry point.) No core/config change required.

## Prior art (herdr plugins)

- **[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)** — closest analog to CodexBar's *Codex* provider. Reads local Codex JSONL at `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (default `~/.codex/sessions`), finds the newest `rate_limits` event, publishes a compact `"78%5h 64%wk"` label into the agents sidebar via a background service, plus a `codex-usage-watch` refreshing pane. **Same on-disk source CodexBar uses for Codex; no OpenAI API call.** Codex-ONLY.
- **[Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard](https://github.com/Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard)** — per-agent token/cost TUI pane (Pi session JSONL + OpenCode server API). Token/cost, not subscription quota.
- **Gap**: no herdr plugin covers **Claude / ChatGPT** subscription quota. CodexBar gets those from OAuth/cookies/CLI, which nothing in the herdr ecosystem mirrors.

## Options when this is picked up

- **A — install the Codex-only plugin** (Effort S): add `herdr plugin install jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit` to the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block pattern in `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (idempotent, mirrors how `cloudmanic/herdr-plus` is installed). Gets Codex quota in the sidebar. Update `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` A–Z + `docs/tools/herdr.md`. **Leaves Claude/ChatGPT uncovered.**
- **B — DIY driver** (Effort M): a small background loop (shell or uv script) that computes `"Claude X% • Codex Y%"` and calls `herdr pane report-metadata … --custom-status` for each agent pane. Data sources, cheapest first:
  1. Reuse **CodexBar's own cached data** — CodexBar reads `~/.codex` (rate_limits) and `~/.claude`; if it caches to `~/.config/codexbar/` or similar, read that instead of re-deriving. (Verify what CodexBar persists; it's a mix of local files + OAuth/cookies/Keychain.)
  2. Codex: read `~/.codex/sessions` rate_limits directly (same as the plugin).
  3. Claude: `~/.claude` usage files if present; else scrape the Claude CLI. Hardest part; may not be cleanly file-derivable.
  - Wire the loop as a herdr `[[keys.command]]` `type="shell"` (detached) entry in `dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, or a pueue/launchd timer. Keep the per-pane `--source` stable so labels update in place.

## Open questions

- What exactly does CodexBar persist to disk (so B.1 is viable vs re-deriving)? Inspect `~/.config/codexbar/` and `~/.codexbar/`.
- Per-pane vs per-workspace: push one rolled-up label per workspace, or per agent pane? `report-metadata` is per-pane, so per-agent is natural but noisier.
- Is this worth it while CodexBar's menu bar already shows everything? Trigger to build: user reports actually living in herdr and wanting to drop the menu-bar glance.

```

All done. Here's what shipped, everything verified against the live herdr server (v0.7.1) with your real workspaces left untouched.

## Built: `hvibe` + `hcode` (herdr analogs of `svibe`/`scode`)

**`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`** — reuses svibe's pure helpers (`_sesh_wrap_agent` specstory-wrap, `_sesh_on_exit_wrap`, `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`) verbatim; only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI calls.

- **`hvibe [N] [CLI]`** / **`hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode`** → workspace `vibe/<repo>` with an `agents` tab (N even-width panes) + `git` (lazygit) + `edit` (nvim) tabs. `--tab-per-agent` puts each agent in its own tab.
- **`hcode [CLI]`** → workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`: `editor` tab (nvim 75% ∣ agent 25%) + `monitor` tab (btop).
- Idempotent per repo, git-gated, same `--on-exit`/`--no-specstory`/`--no-attach` flags. Falls back cleanly if herdr/jq absent.

**Live-verified:** splits give perfectly even columns (51/51/51 for 3 agents), hcode geometry is 75/25, `--tab-per-agent` produces per-agent tabs, and re-running focuses the existing workspace instead of duplicating. Two live-caught bugs fixed along the way — `--ratio` is the fraction kept by the *left* pane (not the new one), and herdr has no even-out command so each split's ratio is computed as `1/(N−m+1)`.

## Your three side questions

- **Sidebar agent panel (one vs many):** herdr tracks agents **per-pane** — two agents in one tab show as **two** separate entries in `herdr agent list`, so the default splits layout surfaces every agent individually. The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot, which is exactly why I added `--tab-per-agent` (each agent → its own tab-level dot).
- **which-key:** already native — `prefix + ?` opens a dynamic "every active binding" overlay. Nothing to build; documented it (confirmed our config doesn't rebind `?`).
- **Accidental-close restore:** yes, two native layers — closing the terminal just detaches (reattach with `herdr`), and `[session] resume_agents_on_restore = true` + pane-history saving restores across a full server restart/reboot (needs the `herdr integration install` hooks). Documented.

## CodexBar-style usage → backlogged (your choice)

```md
# Surface `hvibe`/`hcode` inside herdr's UI (keybinding / tv / Projects)

**Status**: P? — follow-ups to the shipped `hvibe`/`hcode` (2026-07), not spiked
**Effort**: S (keybinding) / S–M (tv action) / S (Projects TOML)
**Related**: `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (`hvibe`/`hcode`), `dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`, [docs/tools/herdr.md](../docs/tools/herdr.md) → "Session helpers"

## Context

`hvibe`/`hcode` currently launch by *typing* the command in a shell. These follow-ups surface the whole-pack layout from **inside herdr's UI** so you don't have to drop to a prompt. All three are additive and independent — pick whichever earns its keep.

Custom herdr commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd — that's the hook for passing "the current project dir" into `hvibe`.

## Option A — keybinding in `create_config.toml`

Bind e.g. `prefix+alt+v` → `hvibe`, `prefix+alt+c` → `hcode`:

\```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+alt+v"
type = "pane"      # temporary pane, closes when the command exits
command = "hvibe -p \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\""
\```

Design calls / caveats:
- `type="pane"` opens a **tiling split**, not a floating popup (herdr issue [#785](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785) — centered float for `[[keys.command]]` is *not planned*; only plugins get `--placement overlay`). The launcher pane is short-lived (hvibe creates + focuses a new workspace, then the launcher pane closes), so the transient split is tolerable — verify it doesn't leave a stray pane behind.
- `hvibe` resolves the git root from `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`; if that pane isn't in a repo, hvibe errors (by design). Consider a `type="pane"` so the error is visible before the pane closes.
- Pick keys that don't collide — `prefix+shift+*` is reserved by herdr built-ins; `prefix+alt+*` is free (same rule as the tmux side). Run `herdr server reload-config` and check `diagnostics` for collisions.
- Aliases don't expand in non-interactive shells — bind the **function name** `herdr-vibe` (or `hvibe` only if the command runs through an interactive `$SHELL -lc`). Safer: `command = "zsh -lic 'hvibe -p \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\"'"` or call `herdr-vibe` directly.

## Option B — tv `herdr-sesh` channel action

The `herdr-sesh` channel's `dir` rows (zoxide frecency) currently Enter → `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir> --focus` (empty workspace). Add a second keybinding (e.g. `Ctrl+V`) that runs `hvibe -p "$ref"` on the selected dir instead — one keystroke from "pick a project" to "full pack". Mirror an `hcode` variant on another key if wanted.
- Edit `[keybindings]` + a new `[actions.vibe]` block in `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml` (dispatch on `kind==dir`).
- Keep the existing Enter (empty workspace) for the "just cd there" case.
- Cross-check the tmux-side `sesh` channel doesn't need the mirror (it uses `svibe`, separate).

## Option C — herdr-plus Projects static TOML

For a **fixed** per-repo layout, add a `~/.config/herdr-plus/projects/<repo>.toml` (chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/`) with explicit tabs/panes — launch via the Projects picker (`prefix+O`). Lowest value: static, no parametric agent count, and `hvibe` already covers the dynamic case. Only worth it for a repo whose layout never varies (e.g. a fixed dev-server + logs + editor set that `hcode`/`hvibe` don't model).

## Recommendation

Ship **A** first (smallest, highest daily payoff — "open the pack" on a hotkey from any pane), then **B** if the zoxide-dir → pack flow gets used. Skip **C** unless a fixed-layout repo actually shows up.
